findings.title: A build without MnemoCode refuses the shared standard SSKR seed-width module
findings.reproduction: Build the Dash Deriver with --exclude mnemocode while its standard SSKR feature remains selected.
findings.expected: Remove MnemoCode panels and operations while standard SSKR keeps the exact shared policy constants it needs.
findings.observed: The selective-no-mnemocode command failed on source/sskr/share-platform.ts, imported for SEED_BYTES by the standard host.
findings.impact: A supported selective build fails to compile. No spending-authority or secret-isolation compromise was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Allow that exact shared input only when the real standard SSKR host is present; preserve negative checks for absent SSKR and unrelated MnemoCode code.
findings.requiredVerification: Compile the affected selective artifact and retain source-graph positive/negative controls.
findings.verificationScope: Source-bound targeted host fixtures and applicable static build gates; no release or real-browser approval.

findings.title: Group values are read repeatedly before byte packing
findings.reproduction: Pass a group whose threshold getter changes after its first read. The original constructor repeatedly validates getters and rereads them for Uint8Array.from.
findings.expected: Capture each threshold/count once, validate that snapshot with CheckedSskrBridge.groupSpecifications, then pack its admitted bytes.
findings.observed: The before-fix test rejected an initially valid snapshot on a later getter read. Source review also establishes that a value changing only during packing can bypass the validated snapshot.
findings.impact: Programmatic group objects can be refused inconsistently or change their packed meaning. UI-created plain records are a narrower case; no recovery loss was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Snapshot the group values and delegate member admission and protocol constants to the shared library.
findings.requiredVerification: Single-read getters, 258/259, fractional/negative/NaN refusals, unchanged Envelope group text and official grouped SSKR controls.
findings.verificationScope: Source-bound targeted host fixtures and applicable static build gates; no release or real-browser approval.

findings.title: Unsupported SSKR selectors are repeated and coerced in host refusals
findings.reproduction: Call SskrCodec.create with the synthetic unknown selector used in sskr-bridge-boundary.test.ts. The before-fix refusal contains that supplied text; object selectors reach String().
findings.expected: Refuse an unsupported selector with an owned stable code and constant safe text, without coercion.
findings.observed: The before-fix fixture failed on selector echo. The original adapter explicitly formatted String(encoding).
findings.impact: A value pasted into the wrong field can be repeated in failure presentation. No network disclosure, real secret or wallet compromise was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the codec's one error catalog and an own-key string admission check.
findings.requiredVerification: Unknown text and object selector privacy controls through the real codec; immutable coded host errors.
findings.verificationScope: Source-bound targeted host fixtures and applicable static build gates; no release or real-browser approval.

findings.title: Host image conversion leaves refused or partial output buffers uncleared
findings.reproduction: The original image converter obtains its rasterizer before the PDF cleanup scope, never clears a rejected multi-page result, and accumulates individual outputs without failure cleanup. Sample conversion also retains its source PDF.
findings.expected: An owner clears the input PDF on every image conversion exit and clears prior outputs/unprocessed PDFs after a later refusal; successful output transfers to its caller.
findings.observed: Source paths lacked those cleanup scopes. The new bounded byte fixtures exercise missing conversion, multi-page refusal, late failure, invalid components and successful transfer without rendering PDFs.
findings.impact: Recovery-bearing temporary bytes can outlive the refused export until garbage collection. This is a memory-lifetime defect, not demonstrated exfiltration; JavaScript erasure remains best effort.
findings.recommendedFix: One MnemoCodeCardFiles owner for conversion, partial file-set cleanup and archive packing.
findings.requiredVerification: Tiny synthetic buffer cleanup and ownership fixtures plus existing page job/plan lifecycle regressions.
findings.verificationScope: Source-bound targeted host fixtures and applicable static build gates; no release or real-browser approval.

findings.title: Candidate-list save failure is labelled as saved
findings.reproduction: Force the download boundary to throw. The old finally block always labelled the disabled button Candidate list saved.
findings.expected: State that saving failed, wipe the list and stop any repeat save of wiped bytes.
findings.observed: The success label was in finally irrespective of download success.
findings.impact: A failed recovery-list download can look successful. The host cannot confirm a browser's eventual filesystem publication, so the new message covers the synchronous save boundary only.
findings.recommendedFix: Set the success label only after the save call; handle the refusal with a safe failure message and keep cleanup in finally.
findings.requiredVerification: The actual controller reports failure, clears bytes and disables its button under a synthetic save refusal.
findings.verificationScope: Source-bound targeted host fixtures and applicable static build gates; no release or real-browser approval.

findings.title: Current-document gate traverses ignored historical audit evidence
findings.reproduction: Run pnpm check after restoring pinned dependencies. The link gate follows AUD-022-evidence/build-review.md into a historical node_modules file which is no longer present.
